title: Location Identifiability
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from child's device can directly identify the child's real-time location, movements, and daily patterns, enabling precise tracking of the child's whereabouts.

title: Unauthorized Location Disclosure
description: GPS data transmitted to backend may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through backend vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls, exposing the child's location to malicious actors.

title: Location Pattern Linkability
description: Regular GPS transmissions create a continuous location trail that can be linked across time to identify routines, frequented locations, and potentially correlate with other personal data sources.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Continuous location tracking of a child may violate GDPR and other data protection regulations regarding children's data, consent requirements, and data minimization principles.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location pings written to the Location History Store could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls on the data store

title: Individual Identification from Location History
description: Stored location data could be used to identify specific individuals and their movements, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Location data is not properly anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Linkability of Location Data with Other Data
description: Location history could be linked with other data sources to create comprehensive profiles of individuals' activities and habits.
assumptions: Location data may be combined with other datasets

title: Inaccurate or Incomplete Location Data
description: Location pings may be inaccurate, incomplete, or contain errors, affecting the reliability of any analysis or services based on this data.
assumptions: GPS or location services may have inherent inaccuracies

title: Linkability of Location Pings to User Identity
description: Location pings forwarded from the Mobile App Backend could be linked to specific user identities or devices, enabling tracking of individual movement patterns across time and space.
assumptions: Location data contains or can be correlated with user identifiers; backend maintains user-device mappings.

title: Identifiability Through Location Pattern Analysis
description: Aggregated location pings could be analyzed to identify individuals through unique movement patterns, routine behaviors, or distinctive geofence interactions.
assumptions: Location data is retained long enough for pattern analysis; sufficient data points exist to create identifiable profiles.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The Geofencing Engine could expose location pings to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, logging, or data sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Geofencing Engine has access to location data; access controls may be insufficient; data may be logged or transmitted to third parties.

title: Manipulation of Location Data During Geofencing Processing
description: Location pings could be altered, tampered with, or falsified during processing in the Geofencing Engine, leading to incorrect zone entry/exit determinations.
assumptions: Geofencing Engine processes location data; data integrity controls may be weak; system could be compromised.

title: Zone Definitions Reveal Family Locations
description: Zone definitions stored in the Family Account Store contain sensitive location information (home, school, friend's house) that could identify specific locations of family members, potentially revealing their daily routines and whereabouts.
assumptions: Zone definitions are stored in a format that preserves location specificity

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Zone Definitions
description: Zone definitions could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls, revealing sensitive location information about family members.
assumptions: Access controls on DS2 are not sufficiently robust

title: Linkability of Zone Data to Individuals
description: Zone definitions read by the Geofencing Engine could be linked to specific individuals or family members, enabling tracking of movement patterns and location history across different zones.
assumptions: Zone definitions are associated with specific user accounts or family members

title: Unauthorized Modification of Zone Definitions
description: The Geofencing Engine could be compromised to allow unauthorized modification of zone definitions, potentially redirecting geofencing alerts or creating false triggers for privacy violations.
assumptions: P2 has write access to zone definitions or can influence DS2

title: Inaccurate or Outdated Zone Definitions
description: Zone definitions may become inaccurate or outdated over time, leading to incorrect geofencing behavior that could either fail to trigger alerts when needed or trigger false alerts, affecting system reliability and user trust.
assumptions: Zone definitions are not regularly updated or validated

title: Linkability of Geofencing Notifications
description: Geofencing arrival/departure notifications could be linked to specific individuals, enabling tracking of movement patterns across multiple zones over time.
assumptions: Notifications contain identifiable information or can be correlated with user accounts

title: Identification of User Locations
description: The geofencing notifications could reveal precise location information about individuals, potentially identifying their presence in sensitive or private areas.
assumptions: Notifications are not properly anonymized or aggregated

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Geofencing notification data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, either through system vulnerabilities or improper access controls.
assumptions: Data transmission or storage lacks adequate security measures

title: Manipulation of Geofencing Notifications
description: Arrival/departure notifications could be tampered with, altered, or forged, leading to false location records or denial of service.
assumptions: Data transmission channel is not properly authenticated or encrypted

title: Usurpation of User Identity
description: An attacker could impersonate a legitimate user to trigger false geofencing notifications, potentially causing confusion or false alerts.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or bypassable

title: Child Profile Identification
description: Child's personal information (name, DOB, school) in the profile can be used to uniquely identify the child, potentially exposing them to targeted advertising, profiling, or unwanted contact.

title: Child Data Disclosure
description: Child's sensitive profile data and geofence zones could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or sharing with marketing partners.

title: Child-Parent Linkability
description: Child's profile data can be linked to the parent's account, creating a comprehensive profile that reveals family relationships and could be exploited for identity theft or social engineering.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: Collecting child's school information and geofence zones may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose of account registration, violating data minimization principles.

title: Backend Data Exposure
description: Mobile App Backend processing child's sensitive data creates risk of internal data exposure through inadequate access controls, logging, or insider threats.

title: Parent Account Impersonation
description: Unauthorized actors could impersonate parents to create false child profiles, leading to identity fraud and potential exploitation of child data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of family account and child profile data
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could disclose sensitive family account and child profile data to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the backend system, insecure APIs, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate security controls on the backend system and potential insider threats or external attackers.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Location Data
description: The mobile app backend may disclose the child's current location or location history to unauthorized parties, including third-party services, advertisers, or malicious actors who gain access to the system.

title: Inference of Child's Sensitive Locations
description: Location data can reveal sensitive information about the child's daily routines, including home address, school, workplace, religious institutions, and frequent destinations, potentially enabling stalking or targeted harassment.

title: Linkability of Location Data with Other Personal Information
description: The child's location data can be linked with other personal information (e.g., name, age, school, family details) to create a comprehensive profile, increasing privacy risks and enabling more precise targeting.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: Unauthorized users or systems may gain access to the child's location data through vulnerabilities in the mobile app backend, insufficient authentication, or compromised credentials.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The system may collect location data more extensively than necessary for the stated purpose of viewing location on a map, potentially including historical data beyond what is needed for the current request.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Location Data Privacy Laws
description: The handling of child's location data may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR, COPPA, or other child-specific privacy laws regarding consent, data retention, and parental controls.

title: Location History Linkability to Individuals
description: Stored location history data can be linked to specific individuals over time, creating detailed movement patterns that reveal personal habits, routines, and sensitive locations.

title: Identifiability Through Location Patterns
description: Location history patterns can uniquely identify individuals even without explicit identifiers, as movement patterns are often distinctive and traceable to specific persons.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: Location history data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient, potentially exposing sensitive personal information to attackers or malicious insiders.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The backend may retrieve more location history data than necessary for the map/history view, violating data minimization principles and exposing unnecessary personal information.

title: Unauthorized Access via Authentication Bypass
description: If authentication mechanisms are weak, attackers could impersonate users to access their location history, leading to privacy violations and potential stalking or surveillance.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Sensitive Location Data
description: Processing location history without proper consent or legal basis may violate GDPR and other privacy regulations, as location data is considered sensitive personal information.

title: Linkability of Child Location Data
description: Location data shared with secondary guardian can be linked to the child's identity and movement patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's daily routines and whereabouts.
assumptions: Secondary guardian has access to location data and may correlate it with other information

title: Identifiability of Child from Location Data
description: The secondary guardian could identify the child's specific location, home address, school, or frequent locations through the shared location data, potentially compromising the child's privacy.
assumptions: Location data is precise enough to identify specific places

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Data
description: The secondary guardian may share the child's location information with unauthorized third parties (e.g., other family members, friends, or malicious actors) without the parent's consent.
assumptions: Secondary guardian may not be trusted or may have malicious intent

title: Location Data Tampering
description: The mobile app backend could potentially alter or manipulate the location data before it reaches the secondary guardian, leading to inaccurate or misleading location information.
assumptions: System vulnerabilities or malicious actors could compromise data integrity

title: Unauthorized Guardian Impersonation
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the parent to invite unauthorized secondary guardians who would then gain access to the child's location data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be weak or bypassed

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Even though data is described as aggregated, sophisticated pattern analysis or cross-referencing with other data sources could potentially link data points back to specific users or small user groups, compromising anonymity.
assumptions: Partner has access to additional data sources or analytical capabilities that could de-anonymize the aggregated data

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Analytics Data
description: The advertising/analytics partner may share or sell the received analytics data to third parties beyond the scope of the original agreement, leading to unintended data exposure.
assumptions: Partner has business incentives to monetize data beyond the stated purpose of funding the free tier

title: Excessive Data Collection for Stated Purpose
description: The usage and engagement analytics shared may contain more detailed information than necessary for the stated purpose of funding the app's free tier, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The data granularity exceeds what is needed for basic analytics and ad targeting

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Processing
description: The advertising/analytics partner may process the received analytics data in ways that violate applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding data transfer, processing, or retention.
assumptions: Partner operates in multiple jurisdictions with varying privacy requirements

title: Location data reveals child's precise whereabouts
description: The child's current location data in the SOS/check-in message can identify their precise physical location, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routine, school, home, or other activities.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: The child's location data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or improper access controls on the Mobile App Backend.

title: Location data linkability with other data sources
description: The location data could be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, social media, other app data) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and activities.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The system may collect more location data than necessary for the stated safety purpose, potentially tracking the child's movements beyond the immediate SOS/check-in context.

title: Non-compliance with children's data protection regulations
description: The processing of children's location data may not comply with GDPR-K or other data protection regulations specifically designed to protect minors' privacy rights.
